title: Latency gap fader and netlink degradation mitigation for region routing
creator: Alicia Park
description: Goal: implement a robust region-selection strategy that smooths transient latency spikes (the "gap") while detecting sustained network degradation (netlink issues) and automatically triggering safe fallback behavior to alternate regions or model variants. This work ties p50 and p95 telemetry into a composite netlink health score used by the routing decision path and augments the existing variant-fallback logic with degradation-aware weight decay. Deliverables: 1) a new composite scoring function (LatencyGapFaderScore) that combines short-window p50, long-window p95, and network-level signals (packet loss, tcp_retransmits, jitter); 2) hysteresis and adaptive smoothing (exponential gap fader) to avoid flip-flopping for brief spikes; 3) integration with the tier-based routing policy so that Dedicated/Downgraded tiers are considered before cross-region fallback; 4) safe rollout plan with canary, synthetic traffic tests, and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Composite score implemented and exposed via /routing/score API for evaluation. 2) Route decisions for synthetic traffic match offline simulation for 95% of cases. 3) Canary region rollout for 10% of traffic shows zero user-facing errors and latency regression < 3% p95. 4) Automatic rollback triggers on sustained >1% error delta or p95 worsening >20% over baseline. 5) Unit and integration tests for score computation and hysteresis logic included.
implementation_notes: Score math: score = w_p50*norm(p50_short) + w_p95*norm(p95_long) + w_net*(loss_norm*L + retrans_norm*R + jitter_norm*J). Default weights: w_p50=0.25, w_p95=0.5, w_net=0.25. Norm uses baseline mean/std per region and min-max clipping at 3 sigma. Gap fader: exponential moving average with alpha dynamically derived from recent variance: alpha = clamp(0.05 + variance_factor*0.45, 0.05, 0.5). Hysteresis window uses separate cool-down timers per region and per tier to avoid oscillation when p95 oscillates. When composite score crosses degrade_threshold, decay region weight by multiplier m(t) = exp(-k * time_in_degraded_state) to prefer alternate regions or cheaper variant. All hyperparams surfaced as config flags in routing-config with runtime feature gate.
testing_plan: 1) Offline replay: run 30 days of production telemetry through the scoring pipeline and produce region-choice diff report vs current algorithm. 2) Synthetic spike scenarios: 5000 simulated requests with induced packet loss jitter; assert stability and expected failover. 3) Load testing: ensure scoring and decision path add <1ms median CPU overhead per request at 20k rps. 4) Canary: enable for a single non-critical customer class and monitor DD dashboards and SLOs for 72 hours.
observability_playbook: Expose: composite_score, p50_short, p95_long, packet_loss_pct, tcp_retransmits, jitter_ms, region_weight, time_in_degraded_state. Create dashboard with trend lines and alert on: composite_score > degrade_threshold for >2m, region_weight < 0.5 for >5m, p95 increase >15% over 15m baseline. Add synthetic canary traffic monitor that reports end-to-end latency and error rate; automatic alert triggers rollback job in the routing control-plane when error delta threshold breached.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit/integration tests and simulation (complete). Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal staging traffic and 1% of traffic in us-west-2 for 48h. Phase 2 (limited prod): 10% of non-enterprise traffic for 72h with extended telemetry retention. Phase 3: global 100% with tiered enable flags and rollback watch. Rollback triggers: sustained p95 regression >20% or error rate delta >1% for 30m.
sim_results: Offline replay on a 30-day production slice predicted 18% fewer cross-region fallbacks (reduction in unnecessary failovers) and a 9% improvement in p95 latency for critical routes under intermittent packet loss scenarios. CPU overhead simulated at 0.7ms median per decision; memory increase negligible. Edge case: when all regions exhibit correlated p95 spikes, the algorithm will preserve current-region affinity unless netlink loss dominates.
acceptance_notes: Design review feedback from Maya Singh: lower default weight on p50 to 0.2 to reduce sensitivity to local jitters. Security feedback: no customer traffic is mirrored to new service; config accessible only to ops role. Performance review from Ethan Zhao: move normalization step to precompute pipeline to avoid hot-path compute.

Check synthetic-canary-latency for the affected region and run the canary replay job to confirm root cause. If netlink metrics show packet_loss_pct > 3% while other regions stable, escalate to infra-networking with trace links and packet captures.
